title: AI-generated catalyst design led to experimentally tested polymerization catalysts
summary: A regression-transformer model fine-tuned on historical ring-opening-polymerization data generated candidate catalysts. Researchers selected synthetically accessible, modified surrogates of one model-generated catalyst for laboratory testing. One surrogate, 5c, reached 60% conversion in 32 minutes for monomer 2a and 100% conversion in 45 minutes for monomer 2d, with reported dispersities of 1.06 and 1.34, respectively. The first ChemRxiv v1 (2022-06-27) described computational generation and recovery of a literature-known catalyst. The experimental results appeared in ChemRxiv v2, posted 2023-02-13, and the 2023 peer-reviewed journal article followed on 2023-06-21. The measured tests concern modified surrogates, not the unmodified generated structure.
ai_technology: Regression Transformer generative model fine-tuned on historical polymerization data represented with Chemical Markdown Language
organization: IBM Research–Almaden; IBM Research–Zurich; ETH Zurich; Arctoris

source_review.scope: Primary ChemRxiv v1/v2 records and linked full v1 PDF for version chronology; primary PubMed Central journal full text for model-to-catalyst relationship and measured outcomes; PubMed metadata for journal publication date and affiliations.

evidence.tested: The journal reports model-derived catalyst 3g and synthetically accessible modified surrogates 5c/5d. Surrogate 5c produced 60% conversion of monomer 2a in 32 minutes (dispersity 1.06) and 100% conversion of monomer 2d in 45 minutes (dispersity 1.34).
evidence.unknown: The tested catalysts were modified surrogates rather than the unmodified model-generated 3g structure. These are laboratory ring-opening-polymerization outcomes, not process-scale or commercial performance. The earlier 2022 v1 reported model generation and literature-known catalyst recovery; the experimentally validated result is reported in v2 on 2023-02-13 and in the later journal article.
evidence.ai_role: A regression transformer generated catalyst 3g from historical polymerization data; researchers tested synthetically accessible modified surrogates 5c and 5d that preserved its endocyclic guanidine motif.
